name: fs-scope-deny-mirror
body:
The acting agent's effective `edit`-action scope is the ordered combination of its opencode 2.x permission rules: the lower-priority configuration loads first, the global rules are appended next, and the agent's own rules are appended last, with the last matching rule winning — an allow rule grants the path and a deny rule revokes it. opencode resolves a path that matches zero rules to `ask`. The fs tools' per-path scope (`apg_rm`/`apg_mv`/`apg_cp`) mirrors that ordered `edit` rule set and applies its OWN fail-closed default: a path matched by zero entries is refused rather than asked, so a zero-match path stays out of a filesystem operation's reach. The tools resolve the rule set and the candidate together in one main-anchored frame, so the fs scope stays within the agent's `edit` scope. A code-writer path that resolves into the main checkout is refused independently.

The fs tools read both allow and deny entries as ordered rules: `opencode-suite/lib/apg.ts` reads the agent's `permissions` array, selects the `edit`-action rules into ordered `{glob, allow}[]` (`editAllowGlobs`, `readAgentEditGlobs`, `agentFsGlobs`), and `fsScopeDecision` decides by the last matching rule (allow permits, deny refuses, and a zero match fails closed to refuse). `opencode-suite/tools/apg_rm.ts`, `apg_mv.ts`, and `apg_cp.ts` consume that ordered rule list. `opencode-suite/agents/agent-builder.md` describes the fs tools' scope as the effective allow-plus-deny scope with last match wins, so a sibling cross-denial holds for the fs tools as it holds for `edit`.
